response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT c.gender AS gender, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Invoices i JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.gender), a AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.cnt * 1.0) AS avg_invoice_count, AVG(g.cnt - a.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM g CROSS JOIN a WHERE g.cnt > a.avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: Invoices are counted as rows in Invoices (each invoice once) joined via Orders to Customers; NULL gender forms its own group via GROUP BY.
If no gender exceeds the average (e.g., all counts equal or no data), the query returns one row with NULL values.
